say.text: Welcome. Today's question sounds simple: what does it mean to define something? Go at your own pace, and pause whenever you like.

show.text: What does it mean to define something?

say.text: Here is our goal. By the end, you can explain why a word can be useful without a perfect definition. You can also tell a working definition from a full explanation.

show.text: Goal 1: Why a word can work without a perfect definition | Goal 2: Working definition versus full explanation

say.text: First, a definition is a short statement of what a word means. It can do one of two jobs.

show.text: Definition

say.text: Job one is to report how people already use a word. Job two is to set a new meaning for a word you are introducing.

show.text: Job 1: report how a word is already used | Job 2: set a new meaning for a word

say.text: Dictionaries do job one. A dictionary such as Merriam-Webster describes how people actually use words. It does not invent rules for them.

show.text: Descriptive dictionary

say.text: Dictionary writers draft definitions from collected examples of real use. They also have to slice a word's meaning into separate senses, and that slicing can be arbitrary. So a dictionary entry is a useful report, not the final word.

show.text: Collect real examples of use | Draft a definition | Divide meaning into senses (sometimes arbitrarily)

ask.q: What does a descriptive dictionary try to do?
ask.right: Record how words are actually used by speakers and writers.
wrong: Decide how words ought to be used, whatever people say.
Prove what a thing really is, once and for all.
Give an exact measurement for every word.
ask.why: A descriptive dictionary reflects real usage rather than imposing rules, as Merriam-Webster explains.

say.text: Scientists often need something sharper. Many ideas can be read in different ways, so a study needs a clear tool. That tool is a working definition.

show.text: Working definition

say.text: A working definition is a tool for a job. It is not a claim that it says everything about the idea. Careful scientists have treated their definitions as provisional tools.

show.text: A working definition is a best-for-now tool, not the whole story.

say.text: The most common working definition is the operational definition. It defines something by exactly how you measure it.

show.text: Operational definition = defined by how it is measured

say.text: Here is an example. Researchers have measured stress using blood pressure, and also using the hormone cortisol. That is two different measuring recipes for one word.

show.text: Stress measured by: blood pressure | Stress measured by: cortisol level

say.text: Physics gives a very exact example. The second is defined as 9,192,631,770 periods of a particular radiation from caesium-133 atoms.

show.text: 9,192,631,770 periods of caesium-133 radiation = 1 second

say.text: That recipe is a choice, and it has changed. Until 1967 the second was based on astronomy. A better way to measure came along, so the recipe changed, and the word 'second' stayed.

show.text: Until 1967: based on astronomy | 1967: caesium atom | 1997: 'atom at rest at 0 K' added | 2019: reworded, same content

say.text: Let's check that idea with one question.

show.text: Quick check: operational definitions

ask.q: Which of these is an operational definition of stress?
ask.right: The level of the hormone cortisol in a person, or their blood pressure.
wrong: The feeling you get when life is too much.
Whatever makes people unhappy at work.
A word that people have used for a long time.
ask.why: An operational definition says precisely how something is measured, and researchers have measured stress with cortisol and blood pressure.

say.text: One physicist, Percy Bridgman, went further in 1927. He said a concept is nothing more than the operations used to measure it.

show.text: "nothing more than a set of operations" (Bridgman, 1927)

say.text: Bridgman later admitted that went too far. Measuring covers only one side of what a word means.

show.text: A measurement is one side of a meaning

say.text: So here is the difference to remember. A working definition tells you how to spot or measure something. An operational definition, by itself, is not an explanation.

show.text: Working definition: how to spot or measure it | Full explanation: what it is and why it happens

ask.q: A study defines stress as a person's cortisol level. What has that definition done?
ask.right: It gives a way to measure stress, but it does not fully explain what stress is.
wrong: It fully explains what stress is.
It proves cortisol is the only possible way to measure stress.
It shows that dictionaries are wrong about stress.
ask.why: Operational definitions are not explanations by themselves. Researchers also use many different measures for one idea, so no single one settles it.

say.text: One more warning. A measuring recipe is just a decision, and a decision can be faulty. A recipe is not good only because it is precise.

show.text: A precise recipe can still be a poor choice

say.text: Now a different problem: words with fuzzy edges. Take the word 'game'. Everyone uses it, and almost no one can define it.

show.text: Game

say.text: Think of board games, card games, ball games and athletic games. The philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein noticed that no single feature is shared by all of them.

show.text: Board games | Card games | Ball games | Athletic games

say.text: He compared games to a family. Build, eye colour, walk and temperament overlap and criss-cross among relatives. No one trait is in everyone, yet we see the family.

show.text: Family resemblance

say.text: So a word can work well without sharp boundaries. We use 'game' every day and understand each other. That is our first goal: useful without perfect.

show.text: Useful without a perfect definition

ask.q: What does 'family resemblance' mean for a word like 'game'?
ask.right: The examples are linked by overlapping similarities, with no single feature shared by all.
wrong: Every game secretly shares one feature that we haven't found yet.
All games were invented by members of one family.
A word with no exact definition cannot be used.
ask.why: Wittgenstein said games have no common feature that makes them all games. They are linked by similarities that overlap, like the features of a family.

say.text: Now three tests for any definition. Does it include too much? Does it leave out too much? Does it go in a circle?

show.text: Test 1: too wide? | Test 2: too narrow? | Test 3: circular?

say.text: Test one: too wide. Say a chair is 'a piece of furniture for sitting'. A bench fits that, but a bench is not a chair. The definition includes too much.

show.text: Too wide: includes things it should not

ask.q: Someone defines a chair as 'a piece of furniture for sitting'. A bench fits this, but a bench is not a chair. Which test does the definition fail?
ask.right: It is too wide, because it includes things that are not chairs.
wrong: It is too narrow, because it leaves out real chairs.
It is circular, because it uses the word 'chair'.
It fails because it is too short.
ask.why: A definition is too wide when it applies to things the word does not apply to. The bench is such a thing.

say.text: Test two: too narrow. A definition of religion that requires a creator would leave out religions with no creator, such as Jainism. The definition leaves out too much.

show.text: Too narrow: leaves out things it should include

say.text: Test three: circular. A circular definition uses the word being defined inside its own definition. For example: 'Happy means being in a happy state.' It tells you nothing new.

show.text: Circular: the word defines itself

ask.q: Which of these definitions is circular?
ask.right: 'Happy means being in a happy state.'
wrong: 'A chair is a piece of furniture for sitting.'
'A second is 9,192,631,770 periods of caesium-133 radiation.'
'Stress is measured by blood pressure or cortisol level.'
ask.why: A circular definition includes the term being defined as part of the definition. Only the first answer does that.

say.text: Here is your checklist. You will use it in every class that follows. Take a moment to read it.

show.text: 1. What is this definition for? | 2. Is it a report of use, or a working (measuring) definition? | 3. Does it include too much? | 4. Does it leave out too much? | 5. Does it go in a circle? | 6. Does it explain, or only point and measure?

say.text: Last check, on our first goal.

show.text: Last check

ask.q: Why can a word like 'game' be useful even with no perfect definition?
ask.right: Its examples are linked by overlapping similarities, so people use it well without one shared feature.
wrong: Because dictionaries have settled its exact edges.
Because every game can be measured the same way.
Because a word is only useful once it is operationally defined.
ask.why: Wittgenstein's family resemblance idea says a word can hold together through overlapping similarities. It does not need sharp boundaries.

say.text: To sum up: a definition has a job. A working definition is a tool and not a full explanation. Fuzzy edges are normal. Next time we use this checklist on energy.

show.text: Next class: Energy, precise to calculate and slippery to explain

other_side.claim: An operational definition is what a scientific concept means.
other_side.other_view: Bridgman put this strongly in 1927. Critics said operations capture only one aspect of a concept's meaning, and Bridgman later admitted the claim went too far. Sophisticated operationists then treated operational definitions as provisional tools, not full meanings.

other_side.claim: Words can work well without sharp definitions, because their uses are linked by family resemblance.
other_side.other_view: Wittgenstein used this idea to reject the search for one shared essence. The philosopher Colin McGinn accepts that games overlap and criss-cross, but argues that 'family' is a poor and merely metaphorical picture of it. In his view the point applies to larger groups too.

other_side.claim: A circular definition is always a failure.
other_side.other_view: Logic guides list circular definitions as a standard fault, because they use the term being defined. One circular-definition theory in the Stanford Encyclopedia argues there is no logical requirement that descriptive definitions avoid circularity. A circular definition can also help someone learn what a word means, even if it is weak as a definition.
